boss62.name: Ford 6.2 Boss V8
facts: 411 hp at 5,500 rpm, 434 lb-ft at 4,500 rpm (premium fuel)
Single overhead cam, 2 valves per cylinder, roller-rocker shafts
4.02 x 3.74 in bore and stroke, 6,210 cc; built at Romeo Engine Plant

issues.x: 2011–2013 F-150s with the 6-speed automatic can suddenly downshift into first at any speed. Ford also recalled certain 2014 F-150s for the same symptom.
issues.fix: Dealers reprogram the powertrain control module; 2013 trucks with the 6.2 needed a second update (19V-433).

issues.x: NHTSA lists no recall on the engine itself for 2010–2014 F-150s. No 6.2 failure pattern is documented in the sources used here.

mod54.name: Ford 5.4 Triton 3V V8
facts: 310 hp at 5,000 rpm, 365 lb-ft at 3,500 rpm (320 hp, 390 lb-ft on E85)
Single overhead cam, 3 valves per cylinder, variable cam timing
2010 only; the 6.2 became the only engine for 2011

issues.x: NHTSA lists one recall for 2010 F-150s, for an interior door handle spring. None covers the engine or transmission.

eb35ho.name: Ford 3.5 EcoBoost HO
facts: Higher boost than the regular F-150 3.5, electric wastegates; 85 hp and 50 lb-ft more
Piston-cooling oil jets, upgraded crank and bearings, two-piece oil pan; port and direct injection

issues.t: 10-speed shift linkage and park pin recalls (2017–2018)
issues.rx: roll ?pin|shift (lever|linkage)|rolled away|won'?t (stay )?in park|(not|wouldn'?t) go into gear
issues.x: On some 2017 F-150s with the 10-speed, the pin holding the shift linkage can fall out. A few 2017–2018 trucks were built without a park roll pin. Either can let the truck roll in Park.
issues.fix: Dealers replace or install the pin (17V-671, 18V-213).

issues.x: On some 2021 F-150s a false low-fluid-pressure code can drop the 10-speed into neutral while driving.
issues.fix: Dealers update the powertrain software (22V-188; some trucks redone under 25V-169).

issues.x: Welds on the high-pressure fuel pump can crack and leak fuel or oil on 5,645 2018 trucks with the 3.5 GTDI. NHTSA's summary does not say whether Raptors are included.
issues.fix: Dealers replace the pump (18V-392). Check the VIN on nhtsa.gov.

issues.x: A misaligned engine cup plug can cause a fast oil leak on some 2024–2025 F-150s with the 3.5 GTDI. NHTSA's summaries do not say whether Raptors are included.
issues.fix: Dealers check the plug and replace it if needed (24V-851, 25V-198). Check the VIN on nhtsa.gov.
